title: Reliability crossover tactical lab — sprint briefing
body:
Purpose and scope

This is the tactical briefing for a two-sprint Reliability Crossover Tactical Lab ("Kinetic Lab") aimed at quickly validating operational patterns for SLOs across the Hosted API, Dedicated,
and Private deployment surfaces. The goal is to produce a repeatable playbook, measurable dashboards,
and a lightweight escalation policy that product teams can adopt without heavy platform changes.

Context / Why now
- Growing customer commitments for SLAs on Dedicated and Private drives need standardized SLO guardrails.
- Observability gaps identified in last incident postmortem: missing synthetic coverage for tail latency and
  incomplete error-tagging from the Serving Runtime.
- Need to demonstrate a minimal runbook + canary policy that reduces time-to-recovery and avoids overcommitting
  node scale for transient spikes.

Primary outcomes for the lab (deliverables)
1) Measurement pipeline: end-to-end SLO measurement from telemetry ingestion to Redwood Console tiles.
   - Prometheus + OTLP metric mapping, SLI extraction queries, alerting rules.
2) SLO definitions for three service classes: control-plane, inference-fast-path, offline-batch.
   - Example targets: inference-fast-path: availability >= 99.95% (30d), p99 latency <= 120ms (95th percentile of request sizes 0-512).
3) Error-budget policy and escalation ladder (automated Slack + PagerDuty playbook).
4) Canary template: traffic split, regressions thresholds, automatic rollback trigger.
5) Playbook drafts: incident play, deliberate degradation plan, dependent-service mitigation steps.
6) Mini-experiments report: two failure-injection scenarios and one load-surge test.

Who should be involved
- SRE (lead): Aisha Patel (owner) — measurement pipeline, runbooks.
- Serving Runtime: Marco Ruiz — instrumentation changes, kv-cache signal tagging.
- Observability: Lina Chen — dashboards, alert rule hygiene, synthetic job templates.
- Platform Eng / Infra: Devon Harris — canary routing, autoscaler knobs.
- Product: Priya Nair (product-hosted-api) — acceptance criteria and customer-impact assessment.
- Solutions Eng (optional): Triage for customer-facing docs and playbook alignment.

Sprint plan (4 weeks)
Sprint 1 (weeks 1–2) — Measure & prototype
- Implement SLI queries for: availability (5xx rate, client-error classification), p99 latency, queue depth for dedicated pools.
- Wire OTLP -> Prometheus recording rules and write initial Redwood Console tiles.
- Create synthetic job runbook (latency and correctness checks).
- Lightweight dependency map for inference-fast-path.
Sprint 1 milestones:
- SLI query set checked in (SRE-4123).
- Synthetic job running every 5m against canary cluster.

Sprint 2 (weeks 3–4) — Harden & run experiments
- Implement simple canary traffic split (5% -> 25%) with rollback triggers based on SLO deltas.
- Run two failure-injection experiments: (A) slow downstream KV cache, (B) transient spike in tokenization service.
- Execute controlled load surge and observe error budget burn rate.
- Finalize escalation ladder and automate PagerDuty routing for SLO breaches.
Sprint 2 milestones:
- Canary template merged and exercised.
- Post-experiment brief with recommendations and playbook version 0.1.

Success metrics
- Measurement coverage: 90% of critical SLI tags present in telemetry.
- False positive alerts reduced: show drop of noise by 30% in lab environment.
- Canary rollback correctly triggered in at least 1/2 experiments where regressions were injected.
- Stakeholder sign-off: product + platform confirm that playbook is actionable for a real customer incident.

Risk register and mitigations
- Risk: Instrumentation changes may require model-owner coordination and cause noise.
  Mitigation: Use feature flags and opt-in canary clusters; coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer-impact simulation.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from low-quality SLIs.
  Mitigation: Start with narrow SLI set, iterate, and gate alerts behind a review checklist.
- Risk: Canary routing interferes with billing/metrics for Dedicated pools.
  Mitigation: Isolate canary in separate billing tag and use internal quotas.

Decision log (living)
- 2026-05-14: Agreed to use OTLP -> Prometheus recording rules as the canonical SLI extraction path (owner: Lina).
- 2026-05-20: Canary rollback threshold set to 5% increase in p99 latency OR 0.5% availability drop relative to baseline (owner: Devon).

Open questions
- What is the default SLO window for customer-facing Hosted API vs. Dedicated customers? 30d vs. 7d? (product to decide)
- How do we surface SLOs and error budgets to customers in Private deployments where the control plane is limited?
- Should the platform automatically throttle noncritical features when error budget < 10%? (safety and UX tradeoffs)

Next steps and immediate action items (this week)
- Aisha: create skeleton SLI queries and PR the recording rules (target: 2026-05-18).
- Marco: add kv-cache latency tag to OTLP spans (target: 2026-05-20).
- Lina: scaffold Redwood Console tiles and confirm telemetry mapping (target: 2026-05-22).
- Devon: prepare canary routing config and test harness (target: 2026-05-25).
- Priya: confirm customer acceptance criteria and escalation thresholds (target: 2026-05-25).

Notes to self (working items)
- Keep experiment artifacts small and reproducible: terraform for lab infra, docker files for synthetic jobs.
- Save experiment logs to a centralized S3 bucket with a canonical naming pattern for postmortem.
- Add a short 'how to adopt' one-pager for product teams after sprint 2.

Appendix: quick reference SLO drafts
- Inference-fast-path availability: 99.95% (window 30d), SLI = fraction of requests with 2xx and token stream success.
- Inference-fast-path latency SLO: p99 <= 120ms (window 7d) for requests <= 512 tokens.
- Control-plane (control APIs): availability 99.9% (window 30d).

If you want to join the kickoff sync on Mon 9:30am PT, reply here and I will add to the calendar.

-- Aisha
